premises.text: Medication adherence is a costly problem in health care today
premises.evidence_span: Medication adherence is arguably the most costly problem in health care today, leading to about $300 billion in costs, $100 billion in lost revenues, and 125,000 deaths in the U.S. alone every year.

premises.text: The AdhereTech bottle collects data on medication usage
premises.evidence_span: Every time the patient uses the bottle, it sends two pieces of data into the cloud. Number one, a time stamp of the open and close of the cap, and number two, a measurement of the amount of medication removed.

premises.text: Interventions are triggered when patients do not take their medications
premises.evidence_span: if we notice a discrepancy, like the patient didn't take their pills, then we intervene, and we intervene in two ways.

premises.text: The bottle is designed to be easy to use and versatile
premises.evidence_span: we were guided by two main philosophies, making it very easy to use and making it extremely versatile.

premises.text: The bottle has a long battery life and is easy to charge
premises.evidence_span: we put a 45-day battery inside of the bottle, so patients don't have to charge it for a standard 30-day prescription.

premises.text: The business model involves partnering with specialty pharma companies
premises.evidence_span: our business model is to partner with specialty pharma companies to distribute high-cost drugs in our bottle.

premises.text: Patients receive the bottle free of charge for certain high-cost specialty medications
premises.evidence_span: Patients will get this bottle from the specialty pharmacy completely free of charge for certain high-cost specialty meds.

premises.text: AdhereTech collects accurate and granular data on medication adherence
premises.evidence_span: we collect the most accurate and granular data out there.

value.text: Patients improve medication adherence and engagement through the use of smart pill bottles
value.evidence_span: we've built a device that will improve the lives of patients.

notes: Partnerships and trial commitments are excluded as traction.
